title: s89: nested-root sessions (<proj> + <proj>/tests) — runner support, scenario, capture
description:
USER INSIGHT 2026-07-22: spawning both s88 agents in the same root does the same thing all other multi-agent scenarios do — it does NOT replicate sessions spawned inside DIFFERENT folders. The correct test: create a project with a repo, spawn an agent there to do work; then (tests being mandatory due to the jot plugin's hooks) spawn a second agent in the project's 'tests/' folder. That produces two separate Claude session project paths: <temp-project> and <temp-project>/tests (e.g. ~/.claude/projects/-private-tmp-scen89-proj and -private-tmp-scen89-proj-tests).

Pieces:
1. RUNNER (jfredToolsPlugin common/scripts/run_scenario_lib.py): support a NESTED declared root (header 'root: tests = /tmp/scen89-proj/tests'). runScenario_launch creates declared roots fresh at launch — nested roots must be created parent-first, and creating/wiping the nested root must not clobber the parent project's content (re-run cleanup wipes the PARENT which contains the nested root — decide create-at-spawn-time vs create-at-launch). Spawn 'SpawnNewAgent: a2 in tests' semantics unchanged; signals stay in the PRIMARY root (existing task-169 behavior).
2. CAPTURE (jfred/run-all-scenarios.py scenario_capture_lib.py): captureCompletedScenario copies JSONLs only from the FIRST jsonl_path's parent project dir — s89 spans TWO project dirs, so the capture must collect every project dir appearing in jsonl_paths, ideally into per-source trees (source-a1/, source-a2/ with projects/ + file-history/ siblings — the layout recorded in jfred/scenarios/executed/s88-multi-source-two-roots/capture-notes.md).
3. SCENARIO s89 (author like task 170, design doc first): a1 in <proj> writes module + tests/ + git repo; a2 spawns in <proj>/tests and edits test files there (paths relative to tests/); interleaved a1/a2 edits on the SAME test file from the two roots; ground-truth ladders; capture + verify like task 171 (prompt approvals via the tmux watcher recipe in memory tasks176-171-159-batch).
4. ENGINE NOTE: nested roots give the SAME file different rel-paths per root (tests/test_x.py under <proj> vs test_x.py under <proj>/tests) — the S5a rel-path identity join (reconstruction_multi_source_join.ts) does not model nested-root absolute-path identity; expect a gap, add the engine test + fix if the merged ladder splits.

description: User workflow: 'start reconstruction from point A (a git hash) up until some chunk of revisions (like 5 or 10 steps), then commit those.
